close_note: Closing lines: ESPN's last pre-game line (DraftKings) for spreads, totals and moneylines; UFC: ESPN's DraftKings closing price for both fighters; props: Locksmith's own last pre-game DraftKings snapshot. When ESPN has no line, the last line Locksmith saw counts only if it was seen within 6 hours of the start (never for UFC); otherwise the bet has no closing number and is counted as missing. Not a sharp (Pinnacle) close: no SharpAPI key is set.
record_note: Every logged ticket counts once, wins and losses: the sport pages' tickets and the Board-only ones, including tickets withdrawn before the start (flagged 'withdrawn'). A second ticket for the same side (flagged duplicate_of) stays in the ledger but is never counted. A side is never logged while the other side of the same game is an open ticket (see conflicts). Changes made to the ledger by hand: see ledger_changes.
ledger_note: No result is ever changed. On Nov 6, 2026 we deleted 12 duplicate UFC tickets (the same fighter logged again when fight ids shifted; 2 were graded, one win and one loss, and the original tickets still count) and flagged 21 bets logged under two ids so each counts once. The ledger from before the cleanup is kept in backups/tracker_pre_fix_0240.

ledger_changes.what: Deleted 12 duplicate UFC tickets. The same fighter on the same card had been logged again each time the card's positional fight ids shifted (next_<event>_<k>); the earliest ticket for each fighter was kept. 2 of the 12 deleted copies were graded (Jacobe Smith, a win, +0.74u; JeongYeong Lee, a loss, -1.50u); both fighters' original tickets are graded and still count. On the 10 kept tickets the withdrawn flag, the last price seen and the start time were refreshed from their copies. The record went from 68-46 (+10.44u) to 67-45 (+11.20u). The same night 45 prop tickets had the player's final stat moved from the closing-line column into the new 'actual' column (no result changed).
ledger_changes.backup: backups/tracker_pre_fix_0240 (the 216-row ledger and its report, from before the cleanup)
ledger_changes.detail: reports/overnight/tracker_cleanup.json (every deleted row and every refreshed field)

ledger_changes.what: No row deleted and no result changed. 21 sides had been logged twice (Nov 3-5), once under the sport page's id and once under the Board's 'B|' id, when a run listed the pick in one place but not the other; 7 of them were graded twice. The later copy of each now carries duplicate_of = the earlier ticket and counts nowhere. The Board-only tickets ('B|'), left out of the headline record until now, count in it. Every graded ticket's close was re-derived: UFC closes now come from ESPN's DraftKings closing price (the old ones were the last price Locksmith saw, 41-44 hours before the fights), and a last-seen line counts as a close only within 6 hours of the start. The headline went from 159 tickets, 68-47, +10.54u to 182 tickets, 74-51, +12.34u (the 21 flagged copies, 6-1 +6.90u, count in neither).

Second opinion -- new 3-model ensemble (better calibrated, not better at picking bets): 69% vs market 57%

nba.summary: Tested 180 rule variants against NBA closing lines/prices with walk-forward side/threshold choice and out-of-sample grading (2021-2026 for most rules, 2025-2026 for betting-split rules). Only 18 of 71 genuine rules with 150+ OOS bets were profitable out of sample and 0 passed the Benjamini-Hochberg FDR test (q=0.10); most rules never even bet because neither side had been profitable in earlier seasons, which is what an efficient closing market looks like. The only 'significant' results (lopsided closing price -> cheap side covers ~68%) come from Action Network price fields that contain post-tip information; they are a data artifact, not an edge. The best OOS result was 'tot_tank' (94/157, ROI +14.3%, t=1.91, 4/5 seasons up), which is not strong enough once ~180 tries are accounted for. No rule survived the full criteria, so the honest conclusion is that this search found no reliable edge against NBA closing lines; live_candidates() returns nothing. Closing lines already price rest, travel, altitude, public money, line moves and recent form; any real edge is most likely at earlier (opening) numbers, not at the close.

wnba.summary: Tested 160 rule variants against WNBA closing lines (spreads/totals at -110, moneylines at the recorded price) with walk-forward side/threshold choice and out-of-sample grading (2020-2026). 18 of 56 rules with 150+ OOS bets were profitable out of sample and 0 passed the Benjamini-Hochberg FDR test (q=0.10). The best OOS result was 'early6_fav' (121/205, ROI +12.7%, t=1.93, 5/6 seasons up), not strong enough once ~160 tries are accounted for. No rule survived the full criteria: this search found no reliable edge against WNBA closing lines, and live_candidates() returns nothing. nhl.summary: Tested 128 NHL betting rules (126 eligible for the significance test, 393 parameter variants) at the closing price, with every threshold/direction chosen on earlier seasons only and results graded out of sample (2022-23 onward). Nothing survived: no rule was significant after the Benjamini-Hochberg multiple-testing correction, so none is recommended. 22 of 117 rules with 150+ OOS bets made money, about what chance plus a ~4% vig predicts; the strongest single result was tot_move_follow1 (+10.8% on 572 bets, one-sided p=0.005), well short of the 0.0008 needed for the top-ranked test. Best OOS returns on 150+ bets: tot_move_follow1 +10.8% (n=572, 4/4 seasons up); tot_juice_under_6.5 +5.3% (n=626, 3/5 seasons up); sch_b2b_fade_travel +3.6% (n=903, 4/5 seasons up). Schedule spots, public-split fades, line-move following, streak/blowout overreaction, goalie news, the favourite-longshot bands and the walk-forward kitchen-sink models all came out at roughly minus the vig: the closing NHL price absorbs this information; the only levers left are getting a better number than the close (betting earlier or shopping books), which these rules do not test.

cfb.summary: Tested 107 CFB hypotheses (254 walk-forward variants), every bet graded at the closing line at -110; none survived Benjamini-Hochberg at q=0.10 (the top-ranked test needed p <= 0.0009; the smallest OOS p was 0.039, W6_gust30_under). Best OOS ROIs with at least 150 bets: T2_level_totalge70 +9.3% on 276 (7/10 seasons up); T22_wind_model_agree +8.7% on 223 (5/8 seasons up); W6_gust30_under +7.2% on 536 (8/10 seasons up). Weather unders (strong gusts, 12+ mph wind) and unders on very high totals are the most persistent positives, but at the close they are a few points of ROI on a few hundred bets a decade, which is not distinguishable from luck across this many tests. Locksmith's own model, line-move, situational (letdown, lookahead, streaks, travel, rest) and favourite/underdog angles are break-even or worse after the vig at the closing price.

ufc.summary: 303 rule variants were tested on 6,647 UFC fights with odds (2015-2026 out of sample), all graded at the closing moneyline. Betting every fighter at the close loses -6.2% (favourites -2.9%, underdogs -9.5%: a mild favourite-longshot bias), and no single-factor angle (price band, debut, age, layoff, streaks, KO losses, reach, stance, weight class, card slot, line movement) survived the false-discovery check. The close alone (log loss 0.6065) is beaten only by walk-forward models that COMBINE it with Locksmith and fighter stats (blend 0.6037, residual logistic 0.6045), and of 254 variants with 150+ bets 54 were positive while 2 passed Benjamini-Hochberg. Survivors: lr_edge_any_4, lr_edge_any_6; the strongest, 'lr_edge_any_6', went 1393-825 (+7.5% ROI, t 3.69, 10/12 years up, last two years +14.6%) and still +4.7% at the worst end of the closing range. The edge is small and comes from many weak pre-fight signals at once (plus favourites being slightly under-priced), so treat it as a modest, price-sensitive edge rather than a lock.

props.summary: Tested 137 NBA/NHL player-prop rules (373 variants scored inside walk-forward training) at the last pre-game DraftKings price on 8146 NBA and 12625 NHL lines with a genuine pre-game close (2026-10-20..2026-11-14 NBA, 2026-10-07..2026-11-14 NHL; the first 2-day block of each is training only). Nothing survives: 0 rule(s) were BH-significant and none met every bar (BH q=0.10, OOS n>=300, ROI>0, 60% of 2-day blocks up). Best by p-value: nba_model_edge_08_both (2201 bets, ROI +6.4%, clustered t 2.55); nba_model_edge (1051 bets, ROI +9.7%, clustered t 2.46); nba_model_edge_05_under (2525 bets, ROI +5.7%, clustered t 2.45). At DraftKings' OPENING price (secondary view) the best rule is nba_model_edge_08_both (7884 bets, ROI +8.4%, clustered t 4.96), which fades to the numbers above at the close -- the line moves toward Locksmith's model, so much of the edge is gone by game time. History is one season (about 1 week NBA, 3 weeks NHL), so even a survivor would be weak evidence; most closing prices are missing because ESPN's latest price for finished games is usually an in-game price.
